interfaces_and_contracts: The README.md section will document the exact interfaces, routes, database tables, and CLI contracts implemented in code: 1. HTTP Routes on Control Plane: POST /rooms/:roomId/events (accepts optional goal on T1 scope.captured up to 20,000 chars with founder_goal SHA-256 digest evidence; refuses task.dispatched.planner, plan.submitted, plan.revision_requested, plan.approved, and founder.cancel with 403 governed_path_required); GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan (authenticated by control-plane read auth; returns the latest T3 plan from build_room_plans with roomState, round, lifecycleEventId, commandId, planHash, and plan, or 409 plan_changed if superseded mid-read); POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision (authenticated by the Phase 3 adjudication credential, 503 when unset; accepts decision values approve, request_revision with feedback, or cancel along with commandId and expectedPlanHash, and commits T5, T4, or T22 plus the journal decision record in one fenced room transaction); POST and GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round and GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal (authenticated by the Phase 4 counted-run credential; inert 503 unless both the credential and PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN surface config are present on Railway with a verified execution-surface-registry.md digest). 2. WebSocket Gateway Planner Protocol: planner_poll (gateway-to-control-plane signed poll carrying gatewayId, timestamp, nonce, and Ed25519 signature) and planner_report (gateway-to-control-plane signed report carrying kind attest, execute, or status and outcome ok, failed, or unknown, plus optional initModel and providerConversationId on execute ok), paired with control-plane planner_work and planner_ack responses. 3. Storage & Journal Contracts: migration 0010_plan_store (public.build_room_plans keyed by command_id with unique (room_id, lifecycle_event_id) and 64-hex plan_hash); build_room_command_journal (BRJ:c:1 / BRJ:c:2 canonical envelopes, sequence numbers, prevRecordHash chain, and advisory lock L4); and PlannerPort (attest, dispatch, awaitPlan, reconcile). 4. CLI & Environment Contracts: npm run phase4:counted-run -- --label <Phase4-CR1|Phase4-CR2|Phase4-CR3> --goal-file <path> (requires PHASE4_EXECUTOR_CONFIRMED set to yes, verifies terms SHA-256, FounderOS checkout cleanliness, remote head SHA, and prior attempt records under <state-dir>/attempts.json and run.lock); gateway daemon env vars BUILDROOM_PLANNER_EXECUTOR (agy or noop), BUILDROOM_AGY_PATH, BUILDROOM_AGY_SHA256, BUILDROOM_PLANNER_USER, BUILDROOM_PLANNER_REPO_MIRROR, and BUILDROOM_PLANNER_WORK_ROOT.
data_flow: The section will trace the end-to-end data flow of a Phase 4 planner round as built: 1. Scope & Goal Capture: A caller posts T1 (scope.captured) to POST /rooms/:roomId/events with scope.paths and an optional goal string; the server validates the goal, rejects credential material, computes its SHA-256 digest, and commits the T1 transition to SCOPED. 2. Round Opening & Journaling: When a planner round is triggered (via PlannerLoop.runRound, invoked on the counted-run surface by POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round), the control plane acquires room lock L3 on a gateway-fenced ledger store. In Round 1 (room in SCOPED), it derives G2 seat facts from roomRoles and the gateway fence, appends T2 (task.dispatched.planner) moving the room to PLANNING, and under journal advisory lock L4 appends the command's journaled record (with deterministic ID cmd_planner_<32-hex> from roomId, openingEventId, and attempt 1..3) in the same Postgres transaction (verified via xmin). On revision rounds (room already in PLANNING after T4 plan.revision_requested) or governed retries after an affirmative not_sent failure within the 3-attempt budget, it journals the next command bound to the opening lifecycle event under L3 and L4. 3. Pre-Dispatch Check, Attestation & Dispatch: Outside the opening transaction, PlannerLoop runs authorizeRoute against the seat registry, requests local seat attestation from the Gateway via PlannerPort.attest (recording identity_bound in the journal), and calls PlannerPort.dispatch over GatewayPlannerChannel. 4. Gateway Execution (AgyPlannerExecutor): GatewayPlannerWorker polls via planner_poll, persists a pending command record in <gatewayDir>/planner, and invokes the configured executor. In agy mode on the designated Linux gateway, AgyPlannerExecutor verifies the root-owned agy binary SHA-256, clones a read-only detached checkout at baseSha, spawns sudo -n -u <plannerUser> -- <agyPath> with pinned flags (--model gemini-4-argon-high --effort high --mode plan --sandbox --print-timeout 900s), waits for the first stream-json init line confirming gemini-4-argon-high and a non-empty conversation_id, writes durable dispatch evidence to <gatewayDir>/planner-evidence before writing the prompt to stdin, collects the single JSON PlanDoc output, and in a finally block kills all processes of <plannerUser> and deletes the checkout. 5. Plan Judgement & Submission: The Gateway reports the dispatched metadata (initModel, providerConversationId) and completed PlanDoc via planner_report. Control plane records dispatched (BRJ:c:2 when initModel/providerConversationId are present), awaits the plan, runs judgeRoundPlan (validating plandoc/1 schema, terminal_status === PLAN_READY_FOR_FOUNDER_APPROVAL, repository, base_sha, scope_paths subset of captured scope, and absence of credential material), and inside one fenced room transaction appends T3 (plan.submitted -> PLAN_REVIEW), inserts the plan into build_room_plans, and appends the journal completed record. 6. Founder Inspection & Decision: The Founder reads the plan via GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan and submits a decision to POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision: approve commits T5 (plan.approved -> APPROVED) plus a journal decision record; request_revision commits T4 (plan.revision_requested -> PLANNING) with feedback digest evidence plus a journal decision record (enabling the next revision round); cancel commits T22 (founder.cancel -> CANCELLED), marks any pending command unresolved before appending the journal decision record, and halts the room.
trust_and_security_boundaries: The README.md section will highlight six enforced trust and security boundaries: 1. Governed Path Enforcement: Raw POST /rooms/:roomId/events refuses all five planner-loop lifecycle events (task.dispatched.planner, plan.submitted, plan.revision_requested, plan.approved, founder.cancel) with 403 governed_path_required so room state cannot advance without matching command-journal and plan-store evidence in the same database transaction (enforced via xmin = pg_current_xact_id()::xid checks). 2. Separation of Credentials: Counted-run orchestration uses the Phase 4 counted-run credential, whereas Founder plan adjudication requires the separate Phase 3 adjudication credential; the Phase 4 run-harness never receives or holds the adjudication credential and pauses at awaiting_founder_decision for an external Founder act. 3. Gateway Fence & Signed Poll/Report: Planner work is dispatched only while the room's gateway lease fence holds, and every planner_poll and planner_report frame is verified against the Gateway's registered Ed25519 public key with replay-window and nonce checks. 4. Sandbox & Process Isolation on the Gateway: AgyPlannerExecutor requires root-owned binary path verification and SHA-256 pinning, executes as an unprivileged dedicated Linux user against a read-only checkout (chmod a-w), withholds the prompt until stream-json init confirms model gemini-4-argon-high and a conversation_id, writes durable evidence before sending the prompt so crash windows fail closed as sent, and unconditionally terminates all planner-user processes (pkill -KILL -u <plannerUser>) and deletes the checkout on exit, writing planner-halted.json if any cleanup or evidence step fails. 5. Credential Redaction & Refusal: Founder goals, revision feedback, journal payloads, and stored PlanDocs are scanned by containsCredentialMaterial; any detected secret material refuses the write before persistence. 6. Inert-by-Default Counted-Run Surface: The counted-run HTTP endpoints return 503 unless the counted-run credential, valid PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN JSON for build-room-control-plane, RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ID, and the hash-pinned execution-surface-registry.md all match.

error_and_failure_behavior: The planned documentation will accurately describe how the built planner loop handles errors and failures: 1. Pre-send vs Post-send Failure Classification: When attestation, authorization, or executor pre-prompt checks fail with affirmative not_sent / never_received evidence, the command is recorded as failed (not_sent) in the journal and PlannerLoop can retry up to MAX_ROUND_ATTEMPTS (3 attempts per opening event, i.e. 1 initial + 2 retries); once retry budget is exhausted or if failure is sent, unknown, or invalid_plan, the round stops without automatic re-dispatch. 2. Crash & Silence Handling: If the Gateway or executor cannot prove not_sent (for example, after pre-prompt evidence is written or when a status check returns unknown), GatewayPlannerWorker stays silent on reconciliation and PlannerRecovery marks or keeps the command in unresolved rather than risking duplicate model execution. 3. Executor Halt Latch: If AgyPlannerExecutor fails to write durable dispatch evidence, fails to reap planner-user processes, or fails to remove the temporary checkout, it writes planner-halted.json in <gatewayDir>/planner-evidence, causing all subsequent executor invocations to refuse with not_sent until operator remediation. 4. Plan Read & Decision Conflicts: GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan re-judges stored plans on read (returning 500 plan_corrupt if tampered) and returns 409 plan_changed if a newer T3 supersedes the plan mid-read; POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision returns 409 on state/command/hash mismatch or 503 when the adjudication credential is not configured. 5. Counted-Run Harness Stop Behaviour: In packages/run-harness/src/phase4, any failed precondition, Round 1 live-check failure (missing init_model or provider_conversation_id on the first command's dispatched row), round failure, or unexpected terminal state persists a terminal failed or blocked record in attempts.json and exits non-zero without automatically starting another attempt.
observability: The README.md section will document the built observability and audit surfaces of the Phase 4 planner loop: 1. Command Journal Chain & Export: Every planner command transitions through hash-chained records in public.build_room_command_journal (BRJ:c:1 and BRJ:c:2 envelopes verified from genesis via JournalStore.verify) and is exported together with lifecycle events via GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal. 2. Live Provider Evidence (BRJ:c:2): When the Gateway executor confirms model initialization, the dispatched journal record captures init_model and provider_conversation_id in its canonical digest input, which the Phase 4 harness verifies during the Phase4-CR1 Round 1 live check. 3. Gateway Local Durable Records: The Gateway persists per-command worker state under <gatewayDir>/planner and per-invocation executor evidence (agySha256, baseSha, initModel, providerConversationId, exitCode, failureKind, and any halt latch) under <gatewayDir>/planner-evidence. 4. Harness Attempt Ledger: The Phase 4 counted-run CLI records every attempt, precondition digest, room ID, round summary, saved plan path, and terminal outcome in <state-dir>/attempts.json guarded by <state-dir>/run.lock.
